state: Incident prep note, 22 Nov 2027, 09:30. On 20 Nov at 16:05 an outside researcher emailed security@ to report that our document app's public share links (/s/{token}) still return a file when the last 4 characters of the token are removed, because the lookup uses a prefix match. The researcher attached two sample links that opened other customers' files: a payroll spreadsheet with staff names and salaries, and a signed contract. The email sat unread in the shared inbox over the weekend; the on-call engineer read it at 09:12 today and reproduced the flaw by 09:25. Code history shows the prefix match shipped in release 3.14 on 2 Oct. Access logs since 2 Oct show 1,840 successful requests using shortened tokens, from 23 distinct IP addresses, 2 of which belong to the researcher. A patch that requires an exact token match is written and tested; deploying it takes 15 minutes. Security policy: confirmed exposure of customer personal data is reported to the privacy officer within 24 hours of confirmation, and affected customers are told within 72 hours of confirmation.

The weather service has issued an amber wind warning for our area from 15:00 to 23:00 today, with gusts forecast at 90-110 km/h.

Our severe weather plan sets response levels by the upper end of the forecast gust range:
- Level 1, gusts up to 60 km/h: normal operations.
- Level 2, above 60 up to 80 km/h: secure loose yard items; stop outdoor work at height.
- Level 3, above 80 up to 100 km/h: Level 2 actions, plus stop yard moves by high-sided vehicles and close windward dock doors.
- Level 4, above 100 km/h: Level 3 actions, plus send non-essential staff home before the warning starts; security and one supervisor shelter in place on site.

The day shift ends at 14:00. The evening shift (38 people) runs 14:00-22:00. Twelve inbound deliveries by articulated trailer are booked between 16:00 and 20:00. Night shift starts 22:00.
